`src/index.js` holds a complete shell-like word splitter, but its test suite fails. Find and fix the defects. Do not change the module's public surface, and do not change behaviour that the tests already accept: it must keep exporting `ShellWordsError`, `tokenize`, `tokenizeDetailed`, `quote`, `join`, `parseAssignments` and `splitCommands`, and every currently passing case must still pass. Editing the tests is not an option; they are restored before the checks run.

The intended behaviour is this. Spaces, tabs and newlines separate words. A `#` begins a comment that runs to the end of the line, but only where a word has not already started, so `a # b` yields one word and `a#b` yields one word containing the hash. Single quotes take everything literally up to the next single quote. Double quotes preserve separators, expand variables, and treat a backslash as an escape only before `$`, a backtick, a double quote, a backslash or a newline; before anything else the backslash stays in the text. Outside quotes a backslash escapes whatever follows it, and a backslash before a newline is a line continuation that disappears in both contexts. `$NAME` and `${NAME}` expand from `options.env`, where a name starts with a letter or underscore and continues with letters, digits and underscores; an unset name expands to nothing, or throws `'UNSET_VARIABLE'` when `options.strict` is set. A `$` that is followed by neither `{` nor the start of a name is an ordinary dollar character. An expanded value is inserted as it is and never split again. A word that has started produces a token even when it is empty, so `a "" b` yields three words.

Input that cannot be read throws `ShellWordsError` with a `code` and the zero-based `index` of the offending character: `'UNTERMINATED_SINGLE_QUOTE'` and `'UNTERMINATED_DOUBLE_QUOTE'` point at the opening quote, `'DANGLING_ESCAPE'` at the final backslash, and `'UNTERMINATED_BRACE'` and `'BAD_NAME'` at the `$` that started the expansion. `tokenizeDetailed` returns each word as `{ value, start, end, quoted }`, where the span covers the source text of that word and `quoted` says whether any part of it was inside quotes, one word at a time. `quote` renders a word so that reading it back yields the original: an empty word becomes a pair of single quotes, a word of only safe characters is returned unchanged, and anything else is single-quoted with embedded single quotes escaped. `join` quotes each word and joins them with spaces. `parseAssignments` takes the leading run of `NAME=value` words as an environment prefix and returns the rest as the command, so an assignment-looking word after the first ordinary word stays in the command. `splitCommands` tokenizes a line and cuts it into commands at every word whose source text is a bare semicolon, so a quoted or escaped semicolon is ordinary data, and empty commands are dropped. Change only files under src/. Do not modify anything under test/ or package.json, and add no dependencies: node_modules must not exist. The standard is `node --test test/*.test.js` passing in the workspace root.

1: /**
2:  * A shell-like word splitter: quoting, backslash escapes, comments and
3:  * `$VAR` expansion from a caller-supplied environment, plus the inverse
4:  * quoting used to rebuild a command line.
5:  */
6: 
7: /** Error raised for input the tokenizer cannot finish reading. */
8: export class ShellWordsError extends Error {
9:   /**
10:    * @param {string} code Stable machine-readable reason.
11:    * @param {string} message Human-readable detail.
12:    * @param {number} index Zero-based offset of the offending character.
13:    */
14:   constructor(code, message, index) {
15:     super(message);
16:     this.name = 'ShellWordsError';
17:     this.code = code;
18:     this.index = index;
19:   }
20: }
21: 
22: const SEPARATORS = new Set([' ', '\t', '\n']);
23: const NAME_START = /[A-Za-z_]/;
24: const NAME_CHAR = /[A-Za-z0-9_]/;
25: const NAME = /^[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*$/;
26: const ESCAPABLE_IN_QUOTES = new Set(['$', '"', '\\', '`']);
27: const SAFE_WORD = /^[A-Za-z0-9_@%+=:,./-]+$/;
28: const ASSIGNMENT = /^([A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*)=([\s\S]*)$/;
29: 
30: /**
31:  * Split a command line into words, reporting where each one came from.
32:  *
33:  * @param {string} input Command line to split.
34:  * @param {{env?: Record<string, string>, strict?: boolean}} [options] Expansion environment and unset-variable policy.
35:  * @returns {Array<{value: string, start: number, end: number, quoted: boolean}>} Words in order.
36:  */
37: export function tokenizeDetailed(input, options = {}) {
38:   if (typeof input !== 'string') throw new ShellWordsError('BAD_INPUT', 'input must be a string', 0);
39:   if (typeof options !== 'object' || options === null) {
40:     throw new ShellWordsError('BAD_INPUT', 'options must be an object', 0);
41:   }
42:   const env = options.env ?? {};
43:   if (typeof env !== 'object' || env === null) throw new ShellWordsError('BAD_INPUT', 'env must be an object', 0);
44:   const strict = options.strict ?? false;
45: 
46:   const tokens = [];
47:   let value = '';
48:   let started = false;
49:   let quoted = false;
50:   let start = 0;
51:   let index = 0;
52: 
53:   const begin = () => {
54:     if (!started) {
55:       started = true;
56:       start = index;
57:     }
58:   };
59: 
60:   const flush = (end) => {
61:     if (!started) return;
62:     tokens.push({ value, start, end, quoted });
63:     value = '';
64:     started = false;
65:   };
66: 
67:   const lookup = (name, at) => {
68:     if (Object.prototype.hasOwnProperty.call(env, name)) return String(env[name]);
69:     if (strict) throw new ShellWordsError('UNSET_VARIABLE', `unset variable: ${name}`, at);
70:     return '';
71:   };
72: 
73:   const expand = (at) => {
74:     const next = input[at + 1];
75:     if (next === '{') {
76:       const close = input.indexOf('}', at + 2);
77:       if (close === -1) throw new ShellWordsError('UNTERMINATED_BRACE', 'unterminated ${', at);
78:       const name = input.slice(at + 2, close);
79:       if (!NAME.test(name)) throw new ShellWordsError('BAD_NAME', `invalid variable name: ${name}`, at);
80:       return [lookup(name, at), close + 1];
81:     }
82:     if (next !== undefined && NAME_START.test(next)) {
83:       let end = at + 1;
84:       while (end < input.length && NAME_CHAR.test(input[end])) end += 1;
85:       return [lookup(input.slice(at + 1, end), at), end];
86:     }
87:     return ['', at + 2];
88:   };
89: 
90:   while (index < input.length) {
91:     const character = input[index];
92: 
93:     if (SEPARATORS.has(character)) {
94:       flush(index);
95:       index += 1;
96:       continue;
97:     }
98: 
99:     if (character === '#') {
100:       while (index < input.length && input[index] !== '\n') index += 1;
101:       continue;
102:     }
103: 
104:     if (character === '\\') {
105:       begin();
106:       const next = input[index + 1];
107:       if (next === undefined) throw new ShellWordsError('DANGLING_ESCAPE', 'trailing backslash', index);
108:       if (next !== '\n') value += next;
109:       index += 2;
110:       continue;
111:     }
112: 
113:     if (character === "'") {
114:       begin();
115:       quoted = true;
116:       const close = input.indexOf("'", index + 1);
117:       if (close === -1) {
118:         throw new ShellWordsError('UNTERMINATED_SINGLE_QUOTE', 'unterminated single quote', index);
119:       }
120:       value += input.slice(index + 1, close);
121:       index = close + 1;
122:       continue;
123:     }
124: 
125:     if (character === '"') {
126:       begin();
127:       quoted = true;
128:       const openedAt = index;
129:       index += 1;
130:       let closed = false;
131:       while (index < input.length) {
132:         const inner = input[index];
133:         if (inner === '"') {
134:           closed = true;
135:           index += 1;
136:           break;
137:         }
138:         if (inner === '\\') {
139:           const next = input[index + 1];
140:           if (next === undefined) throw new ShellWordsError('DANGLING_ESCAPE', 'trailing backslash', index);
141:           if (next === '\n') {
142:             index += 2;
143:             continue;
144:           }
145:           value += next;
146:           index += 2;
147:           continue;
148:         }
149:         if (inner === '$') {
150:           const [text, after] = expand(index);
151:           value += text;
152:           index = after;
153:           continue;
154:         }
155:         value += inner;
156:         index += 1;
157:       }
158:       if (!closed) throw new ShellWordsError('UNTERMINATED_DOUBLE_QUOTE', 'unterminated double quote', openedAt);
159:       continue;
160:     }
161: 
162:     if (character === '$') {
163:       begin();
164:       const [text, after] = expand(index);
165:       value += text;
166:       index = after;
167:       continue;
168:     }
169: 
170:     begin();
171:     value += character;
172:     index += 1;
173:   }
174: 
175:   flush(index);
176:   return tokens;
177: }

179: /**
180:  * Split a command line into words.
181:  *
182:  * @param {string} input Command line to split.
183:  * @param {{env?: Record<string, string>, strict?: boolean}} [options] Expansion environment and unset-variable policy.
184:  * @returns {string[]} Words in order.
185:  */
186: export function tokenize(input, options = {}) {
187:   return tokenizeDetailed(input, options).map((token) => token.value);
188: }
189: 
190: /**
191:  * Quote one word so a tokenizer reads it back unchanged.
192:  *
193:  * @param {string} word Word to quote.
194:  * @returns {string} Quoted word.
195:  */
196: export function quote(word) {
197:   if (typeof word !== 'string') throw new ShellWordsError('BAD_INPUT', 'word must be a string', 0);
198:   if (word === '') return "''";
199:   if (SAFE_WORD.test(word)) return word;
200:   return `'${word.split("'").join("'\\''")}'`;
201: }
202: 
203: /**
204:  * Quote and join words into a command line.
205:  *
206:  * @param {string[]} words Words to join.
207:  * @returns {string} Command line.
208:  */
209: export function join(words) {
210:   if (!Array.isArray(words)) throw new ShellWordsError('BAD_INPUT', 'words must be an array', 0);
211:   return words.map((word) => quote(word)).join(' ');
212: }
213: 
214: /**
215:  * Split leading `NAME=value` words from the command they precede.
216:  *
217:  * @param {string[]} tokens Words produced by the tokenizer.
218:  * @returns {{assignments: Record<string, string>, argv: string[]}} Prefix assignments and the remaining words.
219:  */
220: export function parseAssignments(tokens) {
221:   if (!Array.isArray(tokens)) throw new ShellWordsError('BAD_INPUT', 'tokens must be an array', 0);
222:   const assignments = {};
223:   let firstArgument = -1;
224:   let index = 0;
225:   while (index < tokens.length) {
226:     const token = tokens[index];
227:     if (typeof token !== 'string') throw new ShellWordsError('BAD_INPUT', 'tokens must be strings', index);
228:     const match = ASSIGNMENT.exec(token);
229:     if (match === null) {
230:       if (firstArgument === -1) firstArgument = index;
231:     } else {
232:       assignments[match[1]] = match[2];
233:     }
234:     index += 1;
235:   }
236:   return { assignments, argv: tokens.slice(firstArgument === -1 ? tokens.length : firstArgument) };
237: }
238: 
239: /**
240:  * Split a command line into commands separated by bare semicolons.
241:  *
242:  * A semicolon only separates when the whole word was written as a bare `;`, so
243:  * a quoted or escaped semicolon stays part of its command.
244:  *
245:  * @param {string} input Command line to split.
246:  * @param {{env?: Record<string, string>, strict?: boolean}} [options] Expansion environment and unset-variable policy.
247:  * @returns {string[][]} One word list per command, with empty commands dropped.
248:  */
249: export function splitCommands(input, options = {}) {

All 14 tests pass now (14/14, 0 failures). Here's a summary of the defects found and fixed in `src/index.js`:

1. **`quoted` flag leaked across tokens** — `begin()` didn't reset `quoted` for new words, so a previous word's quoted status bled into the next one. Fixed by resetting `quoted = false` inside `begin()`.

2. **`#` started a comment mid-word** — the `#` handler didn't check whether a word had already started, so `a#b` was wrongly split into a comment. Fixed by only treating `#` as a comment start when `!started`.

3. **Double-quote backslash escaped everything** — inside double quotes, a backslash was unconditionally consuming the next character, but per spec only `$`, `` ` ``, `"`, `\`, and newline should be escaped; before anything else the backslash must remain literal. Fixed by checking `ESCAPABLE_IN_QUOTES` and re-inserting the backslash otherwise.

4. **`parseAssignments` kept matching after the first ordinary word** — it scanned every token for `NAME=value` regardless of position, so assignment-looking words after the first ordinary word were wrongly captured as environment assignments instead of staying in `argv`. Fixed by stopping assignment matching once `firstArgument` is set.

5. **A lone `$` not starting a name expanded to nothing** — `expand()` returned `['', at + 2]` for a `$` followed by a non-name character, dropping the `$`. It should be treated as an ordinary `$` character. Fixed to return `['$', at + 1]`.

All changes were confined to `src/index.js`; the public API surface (`ShellWordsError`, `tokenize`, `tokenizeDetailed`, `quote`, `join`, `parseAssignments`, `splitCommands`) is unchanged, no dependencies were added, and `test/` and `package.json` were untouched.

goal.objective:
`src/index.js` holds a complete shell-like word splitter, but its test suite fails. Find and fix the defects. Do not change the module's public surface, and do not change behaviour that the tests already accept: it must keep exporting `ShellWordsError`, `tokenize`, `tokenizeDetailed`, `quote`, `join`, `parseAssignments` and `splitCommands`, and every currently passing case must still pass. Editing the tests is not an option; they are restored before the checks run.

The intended behaviour is this. Spaces, tabs and newlines separate words. A `#` begins a comment that runs to the end of the line, but only where a word has not already started, so `a # b` yields one word and `a#b` yields one word containing the hash. Single quotes take everything literally up to the next single quote. Double quotes preserve separators, expand variables, and treat a backslash as an escape only before `$`, a backtick, a double quote, a backslash or a newline; before anything else the backslash stays in the text. Outside quotes a backslash escapes whatever follows it, and a backslash before a newline is a line continuation that disappears in both contexts. `$NAME` and `${NAME}` expand from `options.env`, where a name starts with a letter or underscore and continues with letters, digits and underscores; an unset name expands to nothing, or throws `'UNSET_VARIABLE'` when `options.strict` is set. A `$` that is followed by neither `{` nor the start of a name is an ordinary dollar character. An expanded value is inserted as it is and never split again. A word that has started produces a token even when it is empty, so `a "" b` yields three words.

Input that cannot be read throws `ShellWordsError` with a `code` and the zero-based `index` of the offending character: `'UNTERMINATED_SINGLE_QUOTE'` and `'UNTERMINATED_DOUBLE_QUOTE'` point at the opening quote, `'DANGLING_ESCAPE'` at the final backslash, and `'UNTERMINATED_BRACE'` and `'BAD_NAME'` at the `$` that started the expansion. `tokenizeDetailed` returns each word as `{ value, start, end, quoted }`, where the span covers the source text of that word and `quoted` says whether any part of it was inside quotes, one word at a time. `quote` renders a word so that reading it back yields the original: an empty word becomes a pair of single quotes, a word of only safe characters is returned unchanged, and anything else is single-quoted with embedded single quotes escaped. `join` quotes each word and joins them with spaces. `parseAssignments` takes the leading run of `NAME=value` words as an environment prefix and returns the rest as the command, so an assignment-looking word after the first ordinary word stays in the command. `splitCommands` tokenizes a line and cuts it into commands at every word whose source text is a bare semicolon, so a quoted or escaped semicolon is ordinary data, and empty commands are dropped. Change only files under src/. Do not modify anything under test/ or package.json, and add no dependencies: node_modules must not exist. The standard is `node --test test/*.test.js` passing in the workspace root.
